description: Update Cloudflare Worker BACKEND_URL, enhance seed-search.py with sample content, and implement Google identity token authentication in the edge worker for Cloud Run
steps: Step 1 - Update BACKEND_URL in wrangler.toml: Change the production env BACKEND_URL placeholder from 'https://MUST-BE-CONFIGURED.run.app' to 'https://syrabit-backend-851687450401.asia-south1.run.app' in apps/edge/wrangler.toml under [env.production.vars]

Step 2 - Add GOOGLE_SA_KEY to the Env interface: In apps/edge/src/env.d.ts, add an optional GOOGLE_SA_KEY: string field to the Env interface (this will hold the JSON content of the syrabit-edge-invoker service account key, stored as a Wrangler secret)

Step 3 - Create a Google Identity Token utility at apps/edge/src/utils/google-auth.ts: Implement a module that (a) parses the SA JSON from env.GOOGLE_SA_KEY, (b) creates a JWT with iss=client_email, sub=client_email, aud=https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, target_audience=<backend_url>, iat/exp (1hr), signed with RS256 using the SA private key via crypto.subtle, (c) exchanges the JWT for a Google identity token via POST to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer&assertion=<jwt>, (d) caches the token in module-level state with expiry check (refresh 5 min before expiry). Export a function getIdentityToken(env: Env): Promise<string|null> that returns the token or null if GOOGLE_SA_KEY is not configured.

Step 4 - Integrate auth into the API proxy: In apps/edge/src/routes/api-proxy.ts, import getIdentityToken from '../utils/google-auth'. Before making the fetch to the backend, call getIdentityToken(env). If a token is returned, set the 'Authorization' header to 'Bearer <token>' on the outgoing request headers. This ensures the edge worker can authenticate to Cloud Run when allUsers access is blocked by org policy.

Step 5 - Update seed-search.py to include built-in sample educational content: Modify infra/scripts/seed-search.py so that if --data-dir is not provided (make it optional), the script uses a built-in set of sample educational documents (at least 5 documents covering subjects like Mathematics, Science, English, Assamese language, and History) to seed the datastore. Keep the --data-dir option for when users have their own content directory. Add a --sample flag that explicitly seeds the built-in sample content.

Step 6 - Add a unit test for the Google auth module: Create apps/edge/tests/google-auth.test.ts that tests the token generation logic (JWT creation, caching behavior, handling of missing GOOGLE_SA_KEY).
acceptance_criteria: apps/edge/src/env.d.ts Env interface includes GOOGLE_SA_KEY?: string
apps/edge/src/utils/google-auth.ts exists and exports getIdentityToken(env: Env): Promise<string|null>
apps/edge/src/routes/api-proxy.ts calls getIdentityToken and injects Authorization header when token is available
infra/scripts/seed-search.py supports --sample flag for built-in content and --data-dir remains optional
verification: Run 'npx tsc --noEmit' in apps/edge/ to verify TypeScript compiles without errors
Run 'npx vitest run' in apps/edge/ to verify all tests pass including the new google-auth test
Check wrangler.toml contains the correct production BACKEND_URL
Run 'python infra/scripts/seed-search.py --help' to verify the updated CLI interface
findings: 2 pre-existing test failures in tests/deployment-audit.test.ts (JWT-protected endpoint and Rate-limited chat POST tests) - these fail on the base branch without any changes. All new tests pass (7/7 in google-auth.test.ts). TypeScript compiles cleanly.
